title: Job Orchestrator Input Contract
description: Defines all input parameters required to run job-orchestrator. This is the top-level entry point for the AI implementation pipeline.

then.description: implement and analyze start from an issue, so one is required. review and custom have no issue and never did — requiring it unconditionally made two of the four intents unrepresentable.

intent.description: What the job is for. Selects the plan (SKILL.md 1.1) and decides whether `issue` is required.

issue.description: GitHub issue identification. Required for the implement and analyze intents. Provide EITHER url OR repo+number.

path.description: Absolute path to the repository root

base_branch.description: Base branch to create the feature branch from. NO DEFAULT, deliberately: SKILL.md 0.2 auto-detects the repository's own default branch and asks the operator to confirm it. Any value shipped here would be silently inherited by a caller that omits the field, and a branch name is never portable between projects.

additional_codebases.description: Additional codebases for issue-analyzer cross-repo analysis (read-only, implementation happens in primary codebase)

skip_confirmation.description: Must be true — DISPATCHED SUB-AGENTS run without per-dispatch confirmation. It does not govern the Phase 0.4 operator gate ('Proceed?'), which is a question to the human and is controlled by `plan_approval`. The two were read as contradictory only because they shared a name.

max_review_iterations.description: Max review → fix iterations. Three: the same bound `task-implementer`, `flow-orchestrator` and SKILL.md 2.7 carry, pinned across all of them by src/gdskills/round-bound.test.ts. The default was 2 here, which made the contract disagree with the skill it validates.

plan_approval.description: Show the execution plan and ask the operator to approve or adjust before Phase 2 (SKILL.md 1.3). This is the automation switch for an operator question; `skip_confirmation` is not.

auto_create_pr.description: Auto-create draft PR without asking user (default: ask)

review_flags.description: Reviewer selection passed straight to `review-orchestrator` (for example ["--backend", "--security"]). Omit to let it auto-detect from the diff. This replaces the former `reviewers`/`conditional_reviewers` pair, which named individual review skills for a hand-dispatch path SKILL.md 2.6 no longer takes: reviewers are selected by flag and gated by `keryx review stack`, not listed here.

convention_reviewers.description: Optional project-convention reviewers: "ask" (prompt the operator), "all", "none", or a comma-separated list of skill names.

verification_mode.description: Passed to `review-orchestrator` and to `keryx review ingest --verification-mode`. `annotate` records verifier verdicts without removing findings.
